# The hard-surface route: parametric GLB, not generated mesh

> **SUPERSEDED FOR EXECUTION (2026-09-27): use `kiln-route.md`.** Kiln is the
> code-authored GLB route, installed and run end to end here. This file stays for
> the reasoning (why hard surface forks) and the hex-in-material-name technique,
> which Kiln uses.

**Status: UNVERIFIED.** Everything below comes from a public write-up of an AI-built
Roblox FPS (August 2026) plus what the artefacts imply.
Nothing here was run as part of this skill. Treat it as a documented route, not
a proven one. **Check first that your account actually has the 3D/GLB mode of
Claude Design**; a 2D artboard design skill cannot do this.

## The route

1. One asset per conversation page. The source calls this "a critical step" and it is
   just context hygiene: a page carrying a rifle will drag rifle-ness into the
   next object you ask for.
2. Prompt the object. Output is parametric geometry authored as code, so it
   arrives blocky, low poly, hard edged and already inside the MeshPart budget.
3. Iterate in words. "Shrink the stock height" is a real edit here, not a reroll.
   This is the thing the generative pipeline structurally cannot do.
4. Ask for variants explicitly. Because the geometry is code, a variant set
   (bipod yes/no, compact vs long range, arctic / desert tan / blacked out) costs
   one more turn rather than another full generation. For a game that sells skins
   this is most of the value.
5. Download GLB, then Studio's own **Import 3D**.

## The one technique worth writing down: hex in the material name

A parametric GLB carries no textures, so on import the mesh is grey and whatever
is colouring it is guessing from the prompt. The fix is to make the colour
survive the file format:

> tell it to bake the hex colour into each material name

The mesh then arrives with materials named like `eye_1A1A1A`, and whatever wires
it up in Studio reads the intended colour off the name instead of inventing one.

**This does NOT transfer to the Hi3DGen path in this skill.** Hi3DGen returns a
single unsegmented mesh with no materials at all, so there are no names to write
a hex into and no per-part boundaries to apply one to. Do not try to port this
as a fix for the broken stage 4b. It is a property of code-authored geometry.

## Why Import 3D beats this skill's own tail

Stages 5 and 6 of `SKILL.md` need an Open Cloud key (`ROBLOX_API_KEY`) for the
permanent route, or the no-upload `EditableMesh` route for iteration. Studio's
Import 3D is first party and needs neither. On the hard-surface route, clicking
Import is not a downgrade, it is the shortest path with the fewest moving parts.

## The cost

Manual and serial. One download and one import per asset, no batching. That is
fine for the ten or so props an FPS needs and useless for sixteen animals, which
is exactly the line the routing table in `SKILL.md` draws.

## Adjacent trap, not about meshes

The same source generates UI icons on a **magenta** background so the background
keys out cleanly. Magenta sits close to red in chroma, so red and pink elements
in the artwork get partly keyed out along with the background. Its author hit this and
ended up removing backgrounds elsewhere instead. If you use a key colour for
generated 2D assets, measure the worst-case chroma distance against the artwork
first, and never use magenta over anything red.

# Licence audit

Checked 2026-08-24 by reading the actual LICENSE files, not the model cards. That
distinction is the whole reason this file exists: the Hunyuan3D model card was
silent about its territory clause while the LICENSE excluded the UK, EU and South Korea outright.

## The chain this skill depends on

| Component | What it does | Licence | Territory clause |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hi3DGen / Stable3DGen (code) | the pipeline | **MIT**, Copyright (c) 2025 **Bytedance Inc.** | none |
| `Stable-X/trellis-normal-v0-1` | the 3D generation weights | **MIT** | none |
| StableNormal (code) | image to normal map | **Apache-2.0** | none |
| `Stable-X/yoso-normal-v1-8-1` | normal weights | **Apache-2.0** | none |
| TRELLIS (Microsoft) | what Hi3DGen fine-tunes | MIT | none |

**Verdict: clear for commercial use, with no territory clause.** Check the clause against where you live yourself. The authors also removed the
NVIDIA kaolin / nvdiffrast / flexicube dependencies specifically so the adapted
version could be used commercially, which is a deliberate signal rather than an
accident of licensing.

## What is blocked, and stays blocked

**Every Tencent Hunyuan community licence excludes the UK.** Hunyuan3D-2.1,
HY-Motion 1.0 and HunyuanVideo all carry it. Verbatim:

> THIS LICENSE AGREEMENT DOES NOT APPLY IN THE EUROPEAN UNION, UNITED KINGDOM
> AND SOUTH KOREA

and the operative restriction closes the hosted-inference loophole:

> You must not use, reproduce, modify, distribute, or display the ... Works,
> **Output or results** of the Works outside the Territory.

The restriction covers the **output**, so running it on someone else's GPU and
pulling the mesh into a project in an excluded region is still a breach. Do not spend time evaluating
a Tencent Hunyuan model from an excluded region (the UK, EU or South Korea).

## The rule this produced

Read the LICENSE file, not the model card, and not the marketing site. A silent
model card is not evidence of absence: hunyuanmotion.net says "commercial ready"
and says nothing about territory.

## Alternatives, if Hi3DGen ever goes away

- **TRELLIS.2-4B** (Microsoft, MIT) - emits full PBR, outputs GLB, runs on the
  official ZeroGPU Space
- **TripoSR** (MIT) - sub-second, ~6GB VRAM, has a CPU path

# Traps

Symptom first, because that is how you meet them. Everything marked MEASURED was
reproduced while building the skill (Blender 4.3.2, Windows).

---

## 1. The normal map is perfectly flat, and nothing errored - MEASURED

**Symptom.** `normal.png` is a uniform lavender (0.502, 0.502, 1.0). The bake
operator returns `{'FINISHED'}`, the GLB is valid, every other check passes.

**Cause.** The GLB import arrived as a **triangle soup**. glTF stores normals per
corner, so the importer splits every vertex: a welded 10,242-vertex sphere came
back as **61,412 vertices**, and the skill's own test shape went **245,680 ->
40,962** after welding. Nothing is joined to anything, so:

- `Decimate/Collapse` cannot collapse across disconnected faces and under-reduces
  while reporting success
- `Smart UV Project` treats every triangle as its own island and produces
  thousands of sub-pixel islands, so the bake rasterises **no pixels at all** and
  the image keeps its neutral clear colour

**Fix.** Weld immediately after import, before anything measures or reduces:
`customdata_custom_splitnormals_clear()` then `remove_doubles(threshold=1e-5)`.
Clearing the custom normals is part of the fix, not tidying: they hold the
per-face normals that caused the split.

**Why it is worth a whole section.** Three separate wrong diagnoses came first
(operator defaults, `generated_color`, cage extrusion), because a flat map looks
exactly like a cage or selection problem. The bisect that found it swapped a
fresh-built high-poly against an imported one: fresh-high + imported-low failed,
imported-high + fresh-low passed. The **low** poly was the broken one.

---

## 2. `bpy.ops.object.bake` ignores your scene settings - MEASURED

Called from a script, the operator takes its **own property defaults** for
anything not passed explicitly, so `scene.render.bake.use_selected_to_active =
True` is silently ignored and the bake captures the low-poly's own normals: a
perfectly flat, perfectly valid map. Pass every setting as an operator argument
AND set it on the scene. `mesh_pipeline.bake_normal` does both.

(This was not the cause of trap 1, but it is real, and it produces the identical
symptom, which is why it was the first suspect.)

---

## 3. The normal map is soft and washed out - MEASURED

**Cause.** UV padding eating the texture. `island_margin` is charged **per
island**, and a generated mesh unwraps into many islands.

Measured on the test shape at 9,000 triangles, 1024px:

| `--uv-margin` | UV coverage |
|---|---|
| 0.02 | **0.29** |
| 0.003 | **0.49** |
| 0.001 | 0.51 |

0.003 is the default for that reason. Below it you buy almost nothing and start
risking bleed between islands, because the 16px bake margin expands into the gap.
`report.json` carries `uv_coverage`; under 0.25 means look at the layout before
blaming the decimation.

---

## 4. The upload fails with what looks like a permissions error

`assetType: Mesh` takes Roblox-native content only. A `.glb`/`.gltf`/`.fbx` goes
up as **`Model`**. The failure does not say "wrong type", so the next hour goes
into rotating API keys. `upload_asset.py` refuses `Mesh` up front and says why.

---

## 5. The mesh uploads and Roblox rejects it

**20,000 triangles is a hard cap per MeshPart**, enforced at upload. The working
budget is **under 10,000**: 20k is a moderation ceiling, not a performance budget,
and most of Roblox is mobile. `report.json` reports both thresholds separately.

`planar` decimation makes this easy to hit by accident: dissolve merges coplanar
faces and **ignores the triangle target completely**, so a "hard surface" run can
sail past 40k. The pipeline follows planar with a collapse pass for that reason.

---

## 6. Hi3DGen gives you no colour, and that is not a bug - MEASURED

Read from the Space's `app.py`: TRELLIS is called with `formats=["mesh"]` and is
fed the **normal** image produced by StableNormal, not the colour image. So the
GLB has **no texture, no vertex colour and no UVs**. A base-colour bake produces a
flat grey PNG that looks like a failure.

Consequences:

- `Smart UV Project` is mandatory, not cleanup
- colour must come from elsewhere: the concept image, `roblox-texture-gen`, or
  Studio's `generate_material`

---

## 7. Everything is the right shape and the wrong size

Nothing in the chain knows what a stud is. Pass `--target-studs` and state the
size as an intention; otherwise you find out when the crate fills the baseplate.
The pipeline normalises the longest axis and applies the transform **before**
duplicating, because baking across two differently-scaled objects produces
garbage that looks like a UV problem.

**Still unverified:** the exact stud-per-unit factor Roblox applies to an uploaded
GLB, and which way the model faces on import. Check both on the first real asset
and record the answer here.

---

## 8. Twenty instances in and the game starts stuttering

`CollisionFidelity` defaults to `Precise`. On a 10k-triangle mesh that is a
physics trap that shows up long after the import, when nobody connects the two.
Set `Box` or `Hull` at insert time; `references/studio-wire.lua` does.

---

## 9. ZeroGPU refuses the job at hour four

Free ZeroGPU is **300 GPU-seconds per day** against a generation of minutes. That
is a small number of meshes per day, and it fails on **throughput**, not
principle, so it surfaces mid-build rather than at setup. `HF_TOKEN` raises the
quota and buys queue priority; HF PRO ($9/mo) raises it further.

Local generation is not an alternative without a 16GB NVIDIA GPU: a card with
less VRAM, or no CUDA at all, cannot run it at all.

Note the hardware measurement trap while you are here:
`Win32_VideoController.AdapterRAM` is a uint32 and overflows at 4GB. The true
figure is `HardwareInformation.qwMemorySize` in the driver registry key.

---

## 10. Blender 4.x renamed the importers

`bpy.ops.import_scene.obj` no longer exists; it is `bpy.ops.wm.obj_import`. FBX is
still `bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx`, glTF is `bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf`. Tutorials
written for 3.x fail here with a confusing attribute error.

---

## 11. Do not install blender-mcp on the critical path

It ships built-in Hunyuan3D integration, and Hunyuan's licence excludes the UK, EU and South Korea
**including its output**. Reaching for that path silently reimports a licence
breach the model choice was made to avoid. Headless Blender is also deterministic,
where the flaky failures seen while building this skill were all live plugin connections.

---

## 12. `import PIL` fails inside Blender - MEASURED

Blender ships its **own** Python and Pillow is not in it, so anything that runs
under `blender --background --python` must do image work through `bpy`. Load with
`bpy.data.images.load()`, resize with `image.scale(w, h)`, read `image.pixels` as
flat RGBA floats. Values come back **linear, not sRGB**, and row order is
bottom-up, so only compare images that went through the same loader.

Pillow is fine in the scripts that run under the *system* Python
(`batch.py`, `concept_image.py`), which is why the contact sheet lives there.

---

## 13. A silhouette cannot tell left from right - MEASURED

`texture_bake.py --view auto` picks the projection direction by scoring
silhouettes, which removes a convention nobody verified. But a bilaterally
symmetric subject presents **mirror-image profiles**, and those can score
identically: measured on Suzanne, front and back both scored **0.967**.

On livestock the head and tail usually break the tie. When they do not, the run
sets `ambiguous_view: true` and warns, because projecting from the mirrored side
paints **the face onto the rear** - a failure that is obvious in a render and
invisible in every number. Pass `--view` explicitly to settle it.

---

## 14. Kaggle instead of ZeroGPU, and what it costs you

30 GPU-hours per **week** against ZeroGPU's 300 seconds per **day**. Same MIT
weights, same permission, so the venue is purely a throughput decision.

What it costs is indirection: Kaggle has no "run this script on a GPU" endpoint,
so `kaggle_run.py` uploads the concepts as a private **dataset**, uploads the
runner as a private **script kernel** attached to it, and pulls the outputs back.

Four ways it fails, all of them silent-ish:

- **the accelerator is off** - the kernel runs on CPU and exits at the CUDA check
- **internet is off** - the run dies minutes in, at the first weight download,
  long after it looked like it was working
- **the dataset version has not propagated** - a fresh version can take a minute
  to become attachable, so a push-then-run immediately can start with no input
- **the account is not phone-verified** - which is what gates GPU and internet on
  kernels in the first place

Do not pin torch in the kernel. Kaggle ships its own, and reinstalling the version
the Space pins drags half of CUDA with it. Install only the layers on top, and
choose the spconv wheel from the session's actual CUDA version at runtime.

---

## 15. The concept images are poor, and the model is not what you asked for - MEASURED

**Symptom.** Sixteen animals came back soft, malformed and generic: a humanoid
bee, a mangled panda-bull "cow", a pig on a grass platform under a pink sky.

**Cause.** `image.pollinations.ai` was called with `model=flux` and silently
served something else. `GET https://image.pollinations.ai/models` returns
**exactly `["sana"]`** for anonymous callers. SANA is a small fast model, and no
error is raised for asking for a model the tier does not carry.

**Fix.** Default to **FLUX.1-schnell on the official HuggingFace Space**. Measured
on the same cow prompt, the difference is not subtle: correct anatomy, four legs
planted, clean silhouette, plain background, usable first time. Apache-2.0, so
the output is clean for a commercial game (unlike FLUX.1-dev, non-commercial).

**The catch, also measured.** Anonymous callers sit at the bottom of the ZeroGPU
queue. First request 12s, **the very next one refused**: "No GPU was available
after 60s". It is priority, not a hard quota, so `concept_image.py` retries with
backoff - but a batch of sixteen anonymously is an hour of grinding with failures.
`HF_TOKEN` (free account) fixes it, and `kaggle_run.py push --mode images` avoids
the queue entirely by running schnell on your own Kaggle GPU.

---

## 16. A prettier concept image can make a WORSE mesh - MEASURED

FLUX's first output for the cow was a beautiful **flat vector illustration**. It
is the wrong input.

Hi3DGen does not read colour: StableNormal estimates a **normal map** from the
image, and TRELLIS generates geometry from that. Flat cel-shaded art carries
almost no shading gradient to estimate from. Asking instead for a **3D rendered
toy figurine, matte clay surfaces, soft studio lighting, subtle ambient
occlusion** gives the estimator the gradients it needs, and that phrasing is now
baked into `CREATURE_FRAMING`.

Judge a concept by what it gives the normal estimator, not by whether it is a
nice picture.

---

## 17. A reroll silently runs the OLD prompts - MEASURED

Pushing a new dataset version and queueing the kernel in the same breath lets the
kernel attach the **previous** version. MEASURED: a reroll of two animals came
back having regenerated all sixteen, with the previous run's manifest and the
previous run's images, and nothing anywhere said the input was stale. The bee was
still three bees.

`kaggle_run.py push` prints a warning about this, which is not the same as
handling it. Verify the dataset version is current before queueing, or push the
dataset, wait, and push the kernel separately.

Related and worse: `kernels_output` does **not** empty its destination, so files
from a previous run survive and get redistributed as if fresh. On the mesh stage
that quietly overwrites a new GLB with an old one. `fetch` now clears the landing
directory first - by emptying its CONTENTS rather than the directory itself,
because on Windows inside a cloud-synced folder (a sync client) the folder is often locked by the sync client
and `rmtree` dies with WinError 32 after already deleting everything inside.

---

## 18. hi3dgen needs xformers, and the sdpa escape hatch is a trap - MEASURED

The DENSE attention module accepts `ATTN_BACKEND` in
`{xformers, flash_attn, sdpa, naive}`, so setting `sdpa` looks like a clean way to
avoid the xformers/torch version fight.

It is not. The **SPARSE** module accepts only `{xformers, flash_attn}`, silently
ignores anything else, and then runs a bare `import xformers.ops` **at import
time**. The run dies on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'xformers'` after
the full install and the multi-GB weight download.

So xformers must be installed, and pinned to the exact torch that survived the
P100 fix - unpinned, pip satisfies it by upgrading torch and undoes the fix.
Measured pairing: torch 2.5.1 needs xformers 0.0.28.post3.

---

# The Kaggle mesh run: eight attempts, in order

Recorded because every one cost ~15 minutes and every one looked like a different
problem. If you are standing this up again, read the list before you start.

| # | Died at | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `import trellis` | The **Space** uses `trellis`/`TrellisImageTo3DPipeline`; the **repo** ships `hi3dgen`/`Hi3DGenPipeline` |
| 2 | `import xformers` | Sparse attention hard-imports it; `ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa` is silently ignored there |
| 3 | `cumm` ninja build | cumm misdetects the wheel as an editable install |
| 4 | nothing ran | **A bug in the driver script itself**: a patch inserted a `def` mid-body, so `install()` returned before the git clone |
| 5 | `cumm` ninja build | Same as 3, still undiagnosed at that point |
| 6 | `import trimesh` | numpy half-loaded: torch imported in-process *before* the numpy downgrade landed |
| 7 | every asset | `weights/BiRefNet` missing: the repo snapshots weights LOCALLY and loads by relative path |
| 8 | - | **Succeeded.** cow and pig generated; sheep hit CUDA OOM |

## 19. The Space's app.py and the repo's app.py are DIFFERENT - MEASURED

Two separate runs died on this, and it is the single most expensive assumption in
the whole exercise. Copying the HuggingFace Space's `app.py`:

- imports `trellis` and `TrellisImageTo3DPipeline`. The GitHub repo ships the
  package as **`hi3dgen`** with the class **`Hi3DGenPipeline`**.
- loads the pipeline from the HF repo id. The repo instead **snapshots three
  models into a local `./weights` folder** (`trellis-normal-v0-1`,
  `yoso-normal-v1-8-1`, `ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet`) and loads from the local path.

The second one is nastier because it looks like it worked: the pipeline loads, the
GPU spins up, weights download - and then **every asset** fails with
`weights/BiRefNet is not a local folder and is not a valid model identifier`,
which reads like a gated-repo or token problem. It is a **working directory**
problem: BiRefNet is resolved by the relative path `weights/BiRefNet`, so the
process must `chdir` to the repo root.

**Read the repo you are actually cloning, not the demo that inspired it.**

## 20. numpy half-loaded, and every subprocess check passes anyway - MEASURED

Symptom: `ImportError: cannot import name 'broadcast_to' from
'numpy.lib.stride_tricks'`, thrown from a lazy submodule import (trimesh, in this
case) long after startup.

Cause: the driver script called `import torch` in the MAIN process - inside helper
functions computing the spconv tag, the pip constraints and the xformers pin -
which also imports numpy 2.x into memory. The pip downgrade to numpy 1.26.4 then
lands on disk afterwards. The process is left holding 2.x in memory against 1.26.4
on disk.

**The part worth remembering: the import gate went GREEN.** Every check ran in a
fresh subprocess, each saw a consistent 1.26.4, and all four passed - while the
main process died. A subprocess check cannot see the parent's stale imports.

Fix: read torch's version through a subprocess probe, and keep the driver free of
torch and numpy imports until every install has finished. An AST assertion now
fails the push if any function other than `main()` imports torch, numpy or trimesh.

## 21. cumm JIT-compiles because it thinks it is an editable install - MEASURED

`cumm/__init__.py` runs a ninja build when:

```python
project_is_installed(PACKAGE_NAME) and project_is_editable(PACKAGE_NAME) and not CUMM_DISABLE_JIT
```

On Kaggle it misdetects the prebuilt `cumm-cu121` wheel as editable, tries to
compile, and fails inside `pccm`/`ccimport` - naming neither spconv, nor cumm's
install mode, nor CUDA.

Three theories were wrong first, each costing a run: a shadowing source `cumm`
(pip reported both "not installed"), a missing cp312 wheel (one exists), and
numpy 2.x (pinning to 1.26.4 changed nothing). **Reading the failing module's
source settled it in one look.** Set `CUMM_DISABLE_JIT=1` at module scope, before
anything can import cumm.

## 22. Cloning into /kaggle/working makes the weights your OUTPUT

The repo clone and the ~5GB of snapshotted weights land in `/kaggle/working`,
which IS the kernel's output directory. `fetch` then tries to download all of it,

    r = float(span.max()) * 0.06
    for n, colour in ((np.array([1.0, .5, .5]), (1, .05, .05, 1)),

    s.render.film_transparent = True
    s.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
    s.render.image_settings.color_mode = "RGBA"

"""Sample a colour map's ACTUAL pixels against the spec hexes.

Guards the measured 2026-09-02 failure: the painter wrote LINEAR values into a
PNG that is read as sRGB, so a spec asking #969BA0 shipped #4E545A - about half
as bright, which looks like dim lighting and not like a bug. So this reports,
per spec colour:

  present_pct   share of painted texels within tol of the spec colour
  nearest       the closest colour actually in the file, and its distance
  halved_pct    share of texels near srgb_to_linear(spec) - i.e. near the value
                the BUG would have written. Anything but ~0 here is the bug.

Ignores fully-unpainted gutter texels (the painter leaves them at the dilated
edge colour, so a flat-fill check would be dominated by them).
"""
import argparse, json, struct, sys, zlib


def read_png(path):
    d = open(path, "rb").read()
    p, idat, W = 8, b"", None
    while p < len(d):
        ln = struct.unpack(">I", d[p:p + 4])[0]
        tag = d[p + 4:p + 8]
        body = d[p + 8:p + 8 + ln]
        if tag == b"IHDR":
            W, H, bd, ct = struct.unpack(">IIBB", body[:10])
        elif tag == b"IDAT":
            idat += body
        p += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    nch = {0: 1, 2: 3, 4: 2, 6: 4}[ct]
    stride = W * nch
    out, prev, q = [], bytearray(stride), 0
    for _ in range(H):
        f = raw[q]; q += 1
        line = bytearray(raw[q:q + stride]); q += stride
        for i in range(stride):
            a = line[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
            b = prev[i]
            c = prev[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
            if f == 1: line[i] = (line[i] + a) & 255
            elif f == 2: line[i] = (line[i] + b) & 255
            elif f == 3: line[i] = (line[i] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif f == 4:
                pp = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(pp - a), abs(pp - b), abs(pp - c)
                pr = a if (pa <= pb and pa <= pc) else (b if pb <= pc else c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + pr) & 255
        out.append(bytes(line)); prev = line
    return W, H, nch, out


def srgb_to_linear_byte(v):
    c = v / 255.0
    lin = c / 12.92 if c <= 0.04045 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
    return int(round(lin * 255))


ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--png", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--spec", required=True, help='json {"key":"#RRGGBB"}')
ap.add_argument("--tol", type=int, default=14)
ap.add_argument("--step", type=int, default=2)
a = ap.parse_args()

W, H, nch, rows = read_png(a.png)
spec = json.loads(a.spec)

px = []
for y in range(0, H, a.step):
    r = rows[y]
    for x in range(0, W, a.step):
        o = x * nch
        if nch >= 4 and r[o + 3] < 8:
            continue
        px.append((r[o], r[o + 1], r[o + 2]))
n = len(px)

hist = {}
for c in px:
    hist[c] = hist.get(c, 0) + 1
top = sorted(hist.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:6]

res = {}
for k, hx in spec.items():
    t = tuple(int(hx.lstrip("#")[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
    half = tuple(srgb_to_linear_byte(v) for v in t)
    near = sum(1 for c in px if max(abs(c[0] - t[0]), abs(c[1] - t[1]), abs(c[2] - t[2])) <= a.tol)
    nearh = sum(1 for c in px if max(abs(c[0] - half[0]), abs(c[1] - half[1]), abs(c[2] - half[2])) <= a.tol)
    best, bd = None, 1e9
    for c in hist:
        d = max(abs(c[0] - t[0]), abs(c[1] - t[1]), abs(c[2] - t[2]))
        if d < bd:
            best, bd = c, d
    res[k] = {
        "spec": hx.upper(),
        "present_pct": round(100.0 * near / n, 2),
        "nearest_in_file": "#%02X%02X%02X" % best,
        "nearest_chan_dist": bd,
        "halved_value_would_be": "#%02X%02X%02X" % half,
        "halved_pct": round(100.0 * nearh / n, 2),
    }

print("COLOURS " + json.dumps({
    "png": a.png, "size": [W, H], "sampled_texels": n, "tol_per_channel": a.tol,
    "top_colours": [["#%02X%02X%02X" % c, round(100.0 * v / n, 2)] for c, v in top],
    "spec_colours": res,
}))

          --palette '{"shaft":"#5B4632",...}' --out <sheet dir>

WHY. A material can be assigned to real faces, carry the right hex, and still be
painted on ZERO VISIBLE SURFACE because the geometry is buried inside another
part. Every count-based check passes in that state. So this casts rays inward
from a sphere of directions and reports which material the ray actually HITS.

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]

centre = (lo + hi) / 2
radius = (hi - lo).length

# Fibonacci sphere of ray origins; each ray aimed at a jittered point in the bbox

hits = {}
miss = 0
ga = math.pi * (3.0 - math.sqrt(5.0))
import random
random.seed(7)
mw_inv = ob.matrix_world.inverted()
for i in range(N):
    y = 1 - (i / float(N - 1)) * 2
    r = math.sqrt(max(0.0, 1 - y * y))

    d = Vector((math.cos(th) * r, y, math.sin(th) * r))

img = bpy.data.images.load(args.color)
w, h = img.size

def raw_bytes_at(path, x, y):
    """Read the PNG's own sRGB bytes, bypassing Blender's colour management,
    because the failure this guards against is exactly a colour-space one."""
    import zlib, struct
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    p, idat = 8, b""
    W = H = None
    while p < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack(">I", data[p:p + 4])[0]
        tag = data[p + 4:p + 8]
        body = data[p + 8:p + 8 + ln]
        if tag == b"IHDR":
            W, H, bd, ct = struct.unpack(">IIBB", body[:10])
        elif tag == b"IDAT":
            idat += body
        p += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    nch = 3 if ct == 2 else 4
    stride = W * nch
    out = bytearray()
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    q = 0
    for row in range(H):
        f = raw[q]; q += 1
        line = bytearray(raw[q:q + stride]); q += stride
        for i in range(stride):
            a = line[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
            b = prev[i]
            c = prev[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
            if f == 1: line[i] = (line[i] + a) & 255
            elif f == 2: line[i] = (line[i] + b) & 255
            elif f == 3: line[i] = (line[i] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif f == 4:
                pp = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(pp - a), abs(pp - b), abs(pp - c)
                pr = a if (pa <= pb and pa <= pc) else (b if pb <= pc else c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + pr) & 255
        out.extend(line)
        prev = line
    off = (y * W + x) * nch
    return W, H, tuple(out[off:off + 3])


keys = list(palette)
grid = 4
sampled = {}
for i, k in enumerate(keys):

                  "match": ("#%02X%02X%02X" % rgb).upper() == palette[k].upper()}

    "visible_fraction": vis,

"""Stage 5-6 without an upload: pack a MeshPart for Studio to build in place.

    blender --background --python export_for_studio.py -- \\
        --mesh out/low.glb --color out/color.png --outdir serve --name pig

Writes serve/<name>.mesh.bin and serve/<name>.tex.bin, which a local HTTP server
hands to Studio. The plugin rebuilds the mesh through AssetService and needs NO
Open Cloud key, NO ROBLOSECURITY cookie and NO upload of any kind.

AXES. Blender is Z-up, Roblox is Y-up, so every position is rewritten
(x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y). Get this wrong and the animal lies on its side, which
looks like a rig problem and is not one.

COLOUR. Blender hands back LINEAR floats for an sRGB PNG, and Roblox wants sRGB
bytes, so the encode is applied on the way out. Verified by round-trip: the
bytes written here match the source PNG.

FORMAT, little endian, so Luau can buffer.fromstring the body and read it
directly with no base64 and no JSON parse:

  mesh.bin  u32 "RMSH"  u32 version  u32 nVerts  u32 nUVs  u32 nTris
            f32[nVerts*3]  positions, studs, Roblox axes
            f32[nUVs*2]    uv pairs
            u32[nTris*3]   vertex indices
            u32[nTris*3]   uv indices
  tex.bin   u32 "RTEX"  u32 size  u8[size*size*4] RGBA, sRGB
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, struct, sys
from pathlib import Path
import bpy, numpy as np


def args():
    a = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--mesh", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--color")
    p.add_argument("--outdir", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--tex-size", type=int, default=1024)
    return p.parse_args(a)


def linear_to_srgb(c):
    c = np.clip(np.asarray(c, np.float64), 0.0, 1.0)
    return np.where(c <= 0.0031308, c * 12.92, 1.055 * c ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)


def main():
    a = args()
    outdir = Path(a.outdir).resolve()
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=str(Path(a.mesh).resolve()))
    obj = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"][0]
    me = obj.data
    me.calc_loop_triangles()

    nv = len(me.vertices)
    co = np.empty((nv, 3), np.float64)
    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co.ravel())
    mw = np.array(obj.matrix_world.to_4x4())
    co = co @ mw[:3, :3].T + mw[:3, 3]
    # Blender Z-up -> Roblox Y-up
    pos = np.stack([co[:, 0], co[:, 2], -co[:, 1]], axis=1)
    pos = pos - (pos.min(axis=0) + pos.max(axis=0)) / 2.0   # centre on origin

    nl = len(me.loops)
    uv = np.empty((nl, 2), np.float64)
    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv.ravel())

    nt = len(me.loop_triangles)
    tv = np.empty((nt, 3), np.int32)
    tl = np.empty((nt, 3), np.int32)
    me.loop_triangles.foreach_get("vertices", tv.ravel())
    me.loop_triangles.foreach_get("loops", tl.ravel())

    # dedupe UVs so the id space stays small
    quant = np.round(uv * 65535).astype(np.int64)
    _, first, inverse = np.unique(quant, axis=0, return_index=True, return_inverse=True)
    uniq_uv = uv[first]
    tri_uv = inverse[tl]

    # WINDING IS NOT FLIPPED, and that is deliberate. (x,y,z) -> (x,z,-y) has
    # determinant +1, so it is a ROTATION, not a reflection. Flipping the winding
    # "because an axis was negated" renders every face backwards: the mesh looks
    # hollow and see-through with dark patches, which reads as a texture alpha
    # bug and is not one.

    blob = bytearray()
    blob += struct.pack("<4sIIII", b"RMSH", 1, len(pos), len(uniq_uv), nt)
    blob += pos.astype("<f4").tobytes()
    blob += uniq_uv.astype("<f4").tobytes()
    blob += tv.astype("<u4").tobytes()
    blob += tri_uv.astype("<u4").tobytes()
    mesh_path = outdir / (a.name + ".mesh.bin")
    mesh_path.write_bytes(blob)

    size_studs = pos.max(axis=0) - pos.min(axis=0)
    print("[export] {} verts, {} uvs, {} tris -> {} ({:.0f} KB)".format(
        len(pos), len(uniq_uv), nt, mesh_path.name, len(blob) / 1024))
    print("[export] size in studs (Roblox axes X,Y,Z) = {}".format(
        [round(float(v), 3) for v in size_studs]))

    if a.color:
        n = a.tex_size
        im = bpy.data.images.load(str(Path(a.color).resolve()))
        im.scale(n, n)
        px = np.array(im.pixels[:], np.float32).reshape(n, n, 4)
        bpy.data.images.remove(im)
        # DO NOT FLIP THE ROWS. Blender's row 0 is the BOTTOM of the image and
        # Roblox's buffer row 0 is the TOP, but Roblox's UV v also runs from the
        # top while Blender's runs from the bottom. The two conventions cancel,
        # so writing Blender's array as-is samples identically. Flipping it
        # "to correct for bottom-up rows" sends every UV island into the gutter
        # and the model comes back covered in black blotches.
        rgb = (linear_to_srgb(px[:, :, :3]) * 255.0).round().astype(np.uint8)
        alpha = (np.clip(px[:, :, 3:4], 0, 1) * 255.0).round().astype(np.uint8)
        rgba = np.concatenate([rgb, alpha], axis=2)
        tex = bytearray()
        tex += struct.pack("<4sI", b"RTEX", n)
        tex += rgba.tobytes()
        tex_path = outdir / (a.name + ".tex.bin")
        tex_path.write_bytes(tex)
        print("[export] texture {}x{} -> {} ({:.0f} KB)".format(
            n, n, tex_path.name, len(tex) / 1024))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Export a rigged creature as a Roblox-ready SKINNED glb, plus the data the
game needs to pose it.

    blender --background work/rigs/<N>/<N>_rigged.blend \
        --python tools/export_skinned.py -- <N> <outdir>

WHY THIS REPLACES export_creature_parts.py. That script turned the rig into one
BOX per bone and justified it: a skinned MeshPart has to be uploaded before
Roblox accepts bones, and the run could not verify that round trip. The upload
works. The performance argument it was really defending - no Humanoid, no
Animator, one write per frame - never required boxes at all: a Bone.Transform is
a plain property set, so twenty skinned sheep cost 380 property writes at 20Hz,
which is the same order as the BulkMoveTo the boxes needed. The boxes were
throwing away a painted, decimated, normal-baked mesh for nothing.

THE ONE THING THAT IS EASY TO GET WRONG, AND IS COMPUTED HERE RATHER THAN GUESSED:
the axis a gait angle turns about. The gait model says "swing this leg forward by
N degrees". Forward is a direction in the CREATURE's frame; Bone.Transform is
expressed in the BONE's own rest frame, and a Blender bone points along its local
+Y with a roll that is whatever the fitting produced. So a hardcoded
CFrame.Angles(rad(n),0,0) is right for some bones and silently wrong for others -
the kind of defect that reads as "the animation is a bit odd" rather than as a
bug. Instead: take the creature-frame RIGHT axis, express it in each bone's rest
basis, and emit that per bone. The pose code then turns about the axis the rig
says is right, whatever the roll.
"""
import bpy, sys, os, json
from mathutils import Vector, Matrix

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
NAME, OUTDIR = argv[0], argv[1]
os.makedirs(OUTDIR, exist_ok=True)

arm = bpy.data.objects.get(NAME + "_Arm")
mesh = bpy.data.objects.get(NAME)
if arm is None or mesh is None:
    raise SystemExit(f"FATAL: expected objects {NAME} and {NAME}_Arm")

# --- refuse to export something Roblox will reject or render wrong ----------
if not any(m.type == "ARMATURE" for m in mesh.modifiers):
    raise SystemExit("FATAL: mesh has no Armature modifier - it is not skinned")
if not mesh.data.uv_layers:
    raise SystemExit("FATAL: mesh has no UV layer - it would upload untextured")

# Roblox allows at most 4 bone influences per vertex and DROPS the rest without
# a word, which reads as a limb tearing on one specific animation frame.
over = 0
for v in mesh.data.vertices:
    if len([g for g in v.groups if g.weight > 1e-4]) > 4:
        over += 1
if over:
    raise SystemExit(f"FATAL: {over} vertices have more than 4 influences")
unweighted = [v.index for v in mesh.data.vertices
              if not [g for g in v.groups if g.weight > 1e-4]]
if unweighted:
    raise SystemExit(f"FATAL: {len(unweighted)} vertices are bound to no bone")

# --- per-bone swing axis, in the bone's own rest space ----------------------
# Canonical creature frame from the rigger: +Z up, +Y nose, +X right.
RIGHT = Vector((1.0, 0.0, 0.0))
bones = []
for b in arm.data.bones:
    basis = b.matrix_local.to_3x3()
    local_right = basis.inverted() @ RIGHT
    local_right.normalize()
    bones.append({
        "name": b.name,
        "parent": b.parent.name if b.parent else None,
        "swing_axis": [round(c, 6) for c in local_right],
        "head": [round(c, 6) for c in b.head_local],
        "tail": [round(c, 6) for c in b.tail_local],
    })

# --- measured extents. NEVER type an asset bound; the exporter measures. ----
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
ev = mesh.evaluated_get(dg)
pts = [mesh.matrix_world @ v.co for v in ev.to_mesh().vertices]
lo = [min(p[i] for p in pts) for i in range(3)]
hi = [max(p[i] for p in pts) for i in range(3)]

# --- export ----------------------------------------------------------------
for o in bpy.data.objects:
    o.select_set(o in (arm, mesh))
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm

glb = os.path.join(OUTDIR, f"{NAME}_skinned.glb")
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
    filepath=glb,
    export_format="GLB",
    use_selection=True,
    export_yup=True,           # Blender +Z up -> glTF/Roblox +Y up, nose to -Z
    export_skins=True,
    export_animations=False,   # the gait is computed in game, not baked
    export_apply=False,        # applying modifiers would DESTROY the skinning
    export_texcoords=True,
    export_normals=True,
)
if not os.path.exists(glb):
    raise SystemExit("FATAL: exporter reported success but wrote no file")

report = {
    "name": NAME,
    "glb": glb,
    "glb_bytes": os.path.getsize(glb),
    "bones": bones,
    "bone_count": len(bones),
    "verts": len(mesh.data.vertices),
    "tris": len(mesh.data.polygons),
    "extent_min_canonical": [round(c, 4) for c in lo],
    "extent_max_canonical": [round(c, 4) for c in hi],
    "max_influences": 4,
}
with open(os.path.join(OUTDIR, f"{NAME}_skinned.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
print(f"SKINNED_OK {NAME} bones={len(bones)} verts={len(mesh.data.vertices)} bytes={os.path.getsize(glb)}")

"""Centre a creature mesh on its own mass, export, and MEASURE.

The brief: sheep, wolf and dog carry no Humanoid and no rig. They are moved by
BulkMoveTo and animated procedurally from velocity, so an off-centre origin
makes the whole flock orbit its own pivots. mesh_pipeline.py scales but never
centres, so this does it and then measures what came out.

Two centres are reported because they are not the same number:
  bbox centre     - what Roblox re-centres a MeshPart on at import
  vertex centroid - the mass-ish centre; a long tail drags it off the bbox one
The geometry is moved so the BBOX centre is the origin (that is the one Roblox
will use anyway, so anything else drifts) and the residual centroid offset is
reported in studs so the caller can see how far off the mass really is.

  blender --background --python finish_creature.py -- --glb <low.glb>
          --name <Name> --outdir <dir>
"""
import argparse, json, os, sys
import bpy, bmesh
from mathutils import Vector

a = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--glb", required=True)
p.add_argument("--name", required=True)
p.add_argument("--outdir", required=True)
p.add_argument("--bins", type=int, default=12)
args = p.parse_args(a)

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=args.glb)
obs = [o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
assert len(obs) == 1, "expected ONE mesh object (a MeshPart is one mesh), got %d" % len(obs)
ob = obs[0]
ob.name = args.name
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = ob
ob.select_set(True)
bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=True, rotation=True, scale=True)

me = ob.data
bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(me)
xs = [v.co.x for v in bm.verts]; ys = [v.co.y for v in bm.verts]; zs = [v.co.z for v in bm.verts]
centre = Vector(((max(xs) + min(xs)) / 2, (max(ys) + min(ys)) / 2, (max(zs) + min(zs)) / 2))
for v in bm.verts:
    v.co = v.co - centre
bm.to_mesh(me); bm.free()

bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(me)
xs = [v.co.x for v in bm.verts]; ys = [v.co.y for v in bm.verts]; zs = [v.co.z for v in bm.verts]
cen = Vector((sum(xs) / len(xs), sum(ys) / len(ys), sum(zs) / len(zs)))
bm.free()
me.calc_loop_triangles()
tris = len(me.loop_triangles)

# Blender Z-up -> Roblox Y-up is (x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y): determinant +1, a
# rotation, so winding is preserved. Do NOT flip an axis "to compensate".
bounds = [max(xs) - min(xs), max(zs) - min(zs), max(ys) - min(ys)]
bbox_off = [(max(xs) + min(xs)) / 2, (max(zs) + min(zs)) / 2, -(max(ys) + min(ys)) / 2]
centroid_off = [cen.x, cen.z, -cen.y]

# THE ORIENTATION PROFILE, along the long axis, head end first. Printed whole
# rather than reduced to a verdict: three different "which end is the tip"
# rules each inverted on some blade on this project, so hand back the numbers.
body = 1 if (max(ys) - min(ys)) >= (max(xs) - min(xs)) else 0
axco = ys if body == 1 else xs
lo, hi = min(axco), max(axco)
tri_co = [[me.vertices[i].co for i in t.vertices] for t in me.loop_triangles]


def section(c):
    o1, o2 = [], []
    for co in tri_co:
        for i, j in ((0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)):
            p0, p1 = co[i], co[j]
            a0, a1 = (p0.y, p1.y) if body == 1 else (p0.x, p1.x)
            if (a0 - c) * (a1 - c) <= 0 and abs(a1 - a0) > 1e-9:
                t = (c - a0) / (a1 - a0)
                if -1e-9 <= t <= 1 + 1e-9:
                    q = p0 + (p1 - p0) * t
                    o1.append(q.x if body == 1 else q.y)
                    o2.append(q.z)
    if not o1:
        return [0.0, 0.0]
    return [round(max(o1) - min(o1), 3), round(max(o2) - min(o2), 3)]


prof = [section(lo + (hi - lo) * (b + 0.5) / args.bins) for b in range(args.bins)]

os.makedirs(args.outdir, exist_ok=True)
glb = os.path.join(args.outdir, "low.glb")
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=glb, export_format="GLB", use_selection=False,
                          export_apply=True)
obj = os.path.join(args.outdir, "%s.obj" % args.name)
bpy.ops.wm.obj_export(filepath=obj, export_selected_objects=False,
                      export_materials=True, forward_axis="Y", up_axis="Z")

rep = {
    "name": args.name,
    "tris": tris,
    "verts": len(me.vertices),
    "bounds_studs": [round(b, 4) for b in bounds],
    "long_axis_blender": "y" if body == 1 else "x",
    "profile_bins_headfirst_wid_hgt": prof if body == 1 else prof,
    "origin": "bbox centre",
    "bbox_offset_studs": [round(v, 5) for v in bbox_off],
    "centroid_offset_studs": [round(v, 5) for v in centroid_off],
}
with open(os.path.join(args.outdir, "report.json"), "w") as fh:
    json.dump(rep, fh, indent=2)
print("FINISH " + json.dumps(rep))

"""Measure (and optionally yaw) the GLB that is actually uploaded. No Blender.

    python glb_tool.py measure --glb out/low.glb [--bins 10] [--json]
    python glb_tool.py rotate  --glb out/low.glb --yaw 90 [--out rotated.glb]

WHY IT EXISTS (defects it guards, measured on this project):

1. HAND-TYPED BOUNDS DRIFTED UP TO 47%. mesh_pipeline.py's report carries
   `dimensions_studs`, but those are measured on the HIGH poly BEFORE decimation,
   so they are not the numbers of the file that ships. This reads the uploaded
   GLB itself - every primitive, through its node's world matrix - and reports
   the bounds in glTF axes, which are ROBLOX axes (Y up). Put these numbers in a
   manifest, never a typed one.

2. "WHICH END IS THE FRONT" INVERTED ON THREE BLADES under three different rules.
   So `measure` hands back the whole cross-section PROFILE along the longest
   horizontal axis (width across and height per bin), not a conclusion. A second
   reader can check the call from the numbers.

3. AN OPEN MESH IS A SEE-THROUGH HOLE IN ROBLOX (single-sided rendering).
   `measure` welds by position and counts boundary edges (edges with one face).
   Non-zero is reported, not fatal: a generated organic mesh can carry a few.

`rotate` bakes a yaw about the vertical (glTF +Y) into POSITION, NORMAL and
TANGENT and rewrites the accessor min/max, so an asset's front can be put on a
fixed axis IN THE ASSET instead of in a per-asset rotation table in game code
(which goes stale the moment one asset is regenerated). UVs are untouched, so the
painted atlas and the baked tangent-space normal map stay valid.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

CT = {5120: np.int8, 5121: np.uint8, 5122: np.int16, 5123: np.uint16,
      5125: np.uint32, 5126: np.float32}
NC = {"SCALAR": 1, "VEC2": 2, "VEC3": 3, "VEC4": 4, "MAT4": 16}


def load(path: Path):
    data = path.read_bytes()
    magic, _ver, _len = struct.unpack_from("<III", data, 0)
    if magic != 0x46546C67:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path} is not a GLB")
    off, gj, binc = 12, None, None
    while off < len(data):
        ln, typ = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, off)
        body = data[off + 8: off + 8 + ln]
        if typ == 0x4E4F534A:
            gj = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
        elif typ == 0x004E4942:
            binc = bytearray(body)
        off += 8 + ln
    return gj, binc


def save(path: Path, gj: dict, binc: bytearray) -> None:
    js = json.dumps(gj, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
    js += b" " * ((4 - len(js) % 4) % 4)
    bn = bytes(binc) + b"\0" * ((4 - len(binc) % 4) % 4)
    total = 12 + 8 + len(js) + 8 + len(bn)
    out = struct.pack("<III", 0x46546C67, 2, total)
    out += struct.pack("<II", len(js), 0x4E4F534A) + js
    out += struct.pack("<II", len(bn), 0x004E4942) + bn
    path.write_bytes(out)


def accessor(gj, binc, idx):
    acc = gj["accessors"][idx]
    bv = gj["bufferViews"][acc["bufferView"]]
    dt = np.dtype(CT[acc["componentType"]])
    nc = NC[acc["type"]]
    start = bv.get("byteOffset", 0) + acc.get("byteOffset", 0)
    stride = bv.get("byteStride", 0) or dt.itemsize * nc
    if stride != dt.itemsize * nc:
        raise SystemExit("interleaved buffers are not supported")
    arr = np.frombuffer(bytes(binc[start: start + acc["count"] * stride]), dtype=dt)
    return arr.reshape(acc["count"], nc) if nc > 1 else arr, start


def node_matrix(node):
    if "matrix" in node:
        return np.array(node["matrix"], float).reshape(4, 4).T
    t = np.array(node.get("translation", [0, 0, 0]), float)
    x, y, z, w = node.get("rotation", [0, 0, 0, 1])
    s = np.array(node.get("scale", [1, 1, 1]), float)
    r = np.array([[1 - 2 * (y * y + z * z), 2 * (x * y - z * w), 2 * (x * z + y * w)],
                  [2 * (x * y + z * w), 1 - 2 * (x * x + z * z), 2 * (y * z - x * w)],
                  [2 * (x * z - y * w), 2 * (y * z + x * w), 1 - 2 * (x * x + y * y)]])
    m = np.eye(4)
    m[:3, :3] = r * s
    m[:3, 3] = t
    return m


def world_geometry(gj, binc):
    """All triangles of the scene, in world space (glTF = Roblox axes)."""
    verts, tris, base = [], [], 0

    def walk(ni, parent):
        nonlocal base
        node = gj["nodes"][ni]
        m = parent @ node_matrix(node)
        if "mesh" in node:
            for prim in gj["meshes"][node["mesh"]]["primitives"]:
                if prim.get("mode", 4) != 4:
                    continue
                pos, _ = accessor(gj, binc, prim["attributes"]["POSITION"])
                pos = pos.astype(float) @ m[:3, :3].T + m[:3, 3]
                if "indices" in prim:
                    idx, _ = accessor(gj, binc, prim["indices"])
                    idx = idx.astype(np.int64).reshape(-1, 3)
                else:
                    idx = np.arange(len(pos)).reshape(-1, 3)
                verts.append(pos)
                tris.append(idx + base)
                base += len(pos)
        for c in node.get("children", []):
            walk(c, m)

    scene = gj["scenes"][gj.get("scene", 0)]
    for ni in scene["nodes"]:
        walk(ni, np.eye(4))
    return np.concatenate(verts), np.concatenate(tris)


def boundary_edges(v, t, tol=1e-5):
    key = np.round(v / tol).astype(np.int64)
    _, inv = np.unique(key, axis=0, return_inverse=True)
    inv = inv.reshape(-1)
    tt = inv[t]
    tt = tt[(tt[:, 0] != tt[:, 1]) & (tt[:, 1] != tt[:, 2]) & (tt[:, 0] != tt[:, 2])]
    e = np.concatenate([tt[:, [0, 1]], tt[:, [1, 2]], tt[:, [2, 0]]])
    e.sort(axis=1)
    _, counts = np.unique(e, axis=0, return_counts=True)
    return int((counts == 1).sum()), int((counts > 2).sum())


def cmd_measure(a) -> int:
    gj, binc = load(Path(a.glb))
    v, t = world_geometry(gj, binc)
    lo, hi = v.min(axis=0), v.max(axis=0)
    size = hi - lo
    open_e, nonman = boundary_edges(v, t)
    # Long axis = the longer of the two HORIZONTAL Roblox axes (X, Z); Y is up.
    long_ax = 0 if size[0] >= size[2] else 2
    across = 2 if long_ax == 0 else 0
    n = (v - lo) / np.where(size == 0, 1, size)
    prof = []
    for i in range(a.bins):
        m = (n[:, long_ax] >= i / a.bins) & (n[:, long_ax] < (i + 1) / a.bins + (1e-9 if i == a.bins - 1 else 0))
        if m.sum() < 3:
            prof.append({"bin": i, "n": int(m.sum())})
            continue
        s = v[m]
        prof.append({"bin": i, "n": int(m.sum()),
                     "width": round(float(np.ptp(s[:, across])), 3),
                     "height": round(float(np.ptp(s[:, 1])), 3),
                     "y_top": round(float(s[:, 1].max() - lo[1]), 3)})
    has_uv = all("TEXCOORD_0" in p["attributes"]
                 for m in gj["meshes"] for p in m["primitives"])
    out = {
        "glb": str(a.glb),
        "tris": int(len(t)),
        "verts": int(len(v)),
        "bounds_studs_xyz_roblox": [round(float(x), 3) for x in size],
        "longest_studs": round(float(size.max()), 3),
        "centre_offset": [round(float(x), 3) for x in (lo + hi) / 2],
        "has_uv": has_uv,
        "boundary_edges": open_e,
        "nonmanifold_edges": nonman,
        "profile_axis": "XYZ"[long_ax],
        "profile_across": "XYZ"[across],
        "profile_min_to_max": prof,
    }
    print(json.dumps(out) if a.json else json.dumps(out, indent=1))
    return 0


def cmd_rotate(a) -> int:
    src = Path(a.glb)
    gj, binc = load(src)
    ang = math.radians(a.yaw)
    c, s = math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)
    # Right-handed yaw about +Y: x' = c x + s z, z' = -s x + c z
    R = np.array([[c, 0, s], [0, 1, 0], [-s, 0, c]])
    for node in gj["nodes"]:
        if any(k in node for k in ("matrix", "rotation", "scale")):
            m = node_matrix(node)
            if not np.allclose(m[:3, :3], np.eye(3), atol=1e-6):
                raise SystemExit("node carries a rotation/scale; bake transforms before rotating")
    done = set()
    for mesh in gj["meshes"]:
        for prim in mesh["primitives"]:
            for key in ("POSITION", "NORMAL", "TANGENT"):
                idx = prim["attributes"].get(key)
                if idx is None or idx in done:
                    continue
                done.add(idx)
                arr, start = accessor(gj, binc, idx)
                arr = arr.astype(np.float64).copy()
                arr[:, :3] = arr[:, :3] @ R.T
                binc[start: start + arr.astype(np.float32).nbytes] = arr.astype(np.float32).tobytes()
                if key == "POSITION":
                    acc = gj["accessors"][idx]
                    acc["min"] = [float(x) for x in arr[:, :3].min(axis=0)]
                    acc["max"] = [float(x) for x in arr[:, :3].max(axis=0)]
    for node in gj["nodes"]:
        if "translation" in node:
            node["translation"] = [float(x) for x in R @ np.array(node["translation"], float)]
    dest = Path(a.out) if a.out else src
    save(dest, gj, binc)
    print(f"[glb] yaw {a.yaw} deg baked into {dest}")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["measure", "rotate"])
    ap.add_argument("--glb", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--bins", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="one line")
    ap.add_argument("--yaw", type=float, default=0.0, help="degrees about +Y (up)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    return cmd_measure(a) if a.cmd == "measure" else cmd_rotate(a)

"""Dump landmarks for a mesh with the head end STATED, not inferred.

make_paint_spec.py infers the head end from which 8% end-slice has the bigger
cross-section, then --head-end only overrides the FLAG at the end - the
nose_point, nose_z and head_z_range it already computed keep the inferred
answer. On three of this set's four animals the inference was wrong (the rump
out-bulks the head on a round sheep, exactly the cow case in the skill), so
those numbers pointed at the TAIL. This recomputes them from a stated end.

  blender --background --python landmarks.py -- --mesh <low.glb> --head-end min
"""
import argparse, json, sys
import bpy, numpy as np

a = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--mesh", required=True)
p.add_argument("--head-end", choices=["min", "max"], required=True)
p.add_argument("--bins", type=int, default=12)
args = p.parse_args(a)

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=args.mesh)
ob = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"][0]
co = np.array([ob.matrix_world @ v.co for v in ob.data.vertices], dtype=np.float64)
lo, hi = co.min(axis=0), co.max(axis=0)
span = np.where(hi - lo == 0, 1.0, hi - lo)
n = (co - lo) / span
up, body = 2, int(np.argmax([span[0], span[1]]))
width = 1 - body

# body coord with 0 = head, whichever end that is
nb = n[:, body] if args.head_end == "min" else 1.0 - n[:, body]

# THE ORIENTATION PROFILE. Bin along the body axis and report the cross-section
# of each bin, head end FIRST. Printed whole so somebody else can check the
# call instead of taking a verdict on trust.
prof = []
for i in range(args.bins):
    m = (nb >= i / args.bins) & (nb < (i + 1) / args.bins)
    if m.sum() < 3:
        prof.append([0.0, 0.0, int(m.sum())])
        continue
    s = n[m]
    prof.append([round(float(s[:, width].max() - s[:, width].min()), 3),
                 round(float(s[:, up].max() - s[:, up].min()), 3), int(m.sum())])

nose_i = int(np.argmin(nb))
head = n[nb < 0.22]
low = n[n[:, up] < 0.06]
ears = n[(n[:, up] > 0.88) & (nb < 0.35)]

out = {
    "mesh": args.mesh,
    "span_blender_xyz": [round(float(v), 4) for v in span],
    "body_axis": "xyz"[body], "width_axis": "xyz"[width], "up_axis": "z",
    "head_end": args.head_end,
    "profile_head_first_wid_hgt_n": prof,
    "nose_point_xyz": [round(float(v), 3) for v in n[nose_i]],
    "nose_z": round(float(n[nose_i, up]), 3),
    "nose_body": round(float(n[nose_i, body]), 3),
    "head_z_range": [round(float(head[:, up].min()), 3), round(float(head[:, up].max()), 3)],
    "head_width_range": [round(float(head[:, width].min()), 3), round(float(head[:, width].max()), 3)],
    "head_body_z_at_front10": None,
    "foot_body_range_headfirst": [round(float(nb[n[:, up] < 0.06].min()), 3),
                                  round(float(nb[n[:, up] < 0.06].max()), 3)] if len(low) else None,
    "ear_count": int(len(ears)),
    "ear_body_headfirst": round(float(np.median(nb[(n[:, up] > 0.88) & (nb < 0.35)])), 3) if len(ears) else None,
    "ear_z": round(float(np.median(ears[:, up])), 3) if len(ears) else None,
    "centroid_normalised": [round(float(v), 4) for v in n.mean(axis=0)],
}
f = nb < 0.10
if f.sum() > 3:
    out["head_body_z_at_front10"] = [round(float(n[f][:, up].min()), 3),
                                     round(float(n[f][:, up].max()), 3)]
print("LM " + json.dumps(out))

"""Write a first-pass paint spec from measured landmarks and the concept palette.

    blender --background --python scripts/make_paint_spec.py -- \\
        --mesh work/out/low.glb --concept work/concept.png \\
        --out work/pig.paint.json [--name pig]

WHY. Hand-authoring a spec per animal was the one step that did not scale: the
pig took axes_probe, then --describe, then three look-and-adjust passes. But
almost everything used in that hand pass is already MEASURABLE - the body axis,
which end the head is on, where the legs are, how tall the head is - and the
colours are already in the concept. This writes the spec those measurements
imply, so the human pass becomes a CHECK rather than authoring from scratch.

It will not beat a hand-tuned spec. It gets close enough that a render-and-look
is usually the only thing left.

WHICH END IS THE HEAD. The body axis is the longest horizontal one, which is
reliable. WHICH END the head is on is NOT reliably derivable from geometry, and
this is the one thing the generator cannot finish on its own.

The obvious heuristic - a head is bulky, a tail is thin, so compare the
cross-section at the two extremities - works on a pig (11.3x, correct) and FAILS
ON A COW (2.3x, and it picked the wrong end). A cow's rump out-bulks its head;
a pig's does not. Width does not separate them either, and in opposite
directions: the pig's head region is WIDER than its rump, the cow's is narrower.
Two animals, two contradictions, so the heuristic is a tiebreak at best.

So `--head-end auto` is REFUSED below --min-confidence (default 5x, chosen
because the pig cleared it at 11.3x and the wrong cow answer sat at 2.3x). Pass
`--head-end min|max` explicitly. Read it off scripts/axes_probe.py, which is one
render and unambiguous - and for a batch, `batch.py orient` renders every asset
onto ONE contact sheet so the whole set is settled in a single look.

PATTERNED ANIMALS. If the palette holds a second common cluster far from the
base in luminance - a Holstein's black on white - a deterministic scatter of
patch blobs is added. Without it the cow came out ALL WHITE: a clean model of
the wrong animal. The scatter is fixed, not random, so a set regenerates
identically; move or delete the patch stamps by hand if a specific animal needs
specific markings.

COLOUR. The k-means palette of the concept is dominated by SHADED body colour,
not albedo: the pig's most common cluster was #B48E9A, a dull mauve, while the
albedo that reads correctly in engine is nearer #F4AEC8. So the base is the
dominant cluster's HUE, with saturation lifted and value pulled most of the way
toward the brightest cluster. Calibrated against the hand-authored pig spec.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, colorsys, json, sys
from pathlib import Path

import bpy, numpy as np

SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPTS))
import paint_texture as P  # noqa: E402


def args():
    a = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--mesh", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--concept", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--name", default="asset")
    p.add_argument("--clusters", type=int, default=6)
    p.add_argument("--head-end", choices=["auto", "min", "max"], default="auto",
                   help="which end of the body axis the head is on. 'auto' is a "
                        "GUESS and is refused when it is not confident.")
    p.add_argument("--min-confidence", type=float, default=5.0)
    p.add_argument("--preset", default="creature", choices=["creature", "prop"],
                   help="creature emits anatomical stamps (belly, snout, eyes). "
                        "prop emits a flat base colour and NOTHING else - see "
                        "build_prop_spec for why guessing is worse than nothing.")
    return p.parse_args(a)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- colour
def _hex(rgb_srgb):
    return "#" + "".join("{:02X}".format(int(round(max(0.0, min(1.0, c)) * 255)))
                         for c in rgb_srgb)


def _srgb(linear):
    c = np.clip(np.asarray(linear, np.float64), 0, 1)
    return np.where(c <= 0.0031308, c * 12.92, 1.055 * c ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)


def _shift(rgb, dv=0.0, ds=0.0, dh=0.0):
    h, s, v = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*[float(x) for x in rgb])
    return colorsys.hsv_to_rgb((h + dh) % 1.0, max(0.0, min(1.0, s + ds)),
                               max(0.0, min(1.0, v + dv)))


def palette(concept: Path, k: int):
    """Subject-only k-means, using the flood-fill mask. A chroma test is not
    enough: a grey backdrop picks up a colour cast off the subject."""
    mask, rgb = P.subject_mask(concept, 256)
    P.check_mask(mask)
    keep = rgb[mask]

    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    cen = keep[rng.choice(len(keep), k, replace=False)]
    lab = np.zeros(len(keep), int)
    for _ in range(30):
        d = ((keep[:, None, :] - cen[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2)
        lab = d.argmin(axis=1)
        for i in range(k):
            if (lab == i).any():
                cen[i] = keep[lab == i].mean(axis=0)
    shares = np.array([(lab == i).sum() for i in range(k)], float) / len(keep)
    srgb = np.array([_srgb(c) for c in cen])
    lum = srgb @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])
    return srgb, shares, lum


def choose_colours(srgb, shares, lum):
    dom_i = int(np.argmax(shares))
    dom = srgb[dom_i]
    brightest = srgb[int(np.argmax(lum))]
    darkest = srgb[int(np.argmin(lum))]

    # Lift the dominant (shaded) cluster toward albedo. See module docstring.
    h, s, v = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*[float(x) for x in dom])
    _, _, vb = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*[float(x) for x in brightest])
    base = colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(h, min(1.0, s * 1.30), v + (vb - v) * 0.70)

    # A PATTERNED animal has a second colour that is common AND far from the
    # base in luminance - a Holstein's black on white. Bands and blobs alone
    # produced an all-white cow, which is a plausible model of the wrong animal.
    base_lum = float(np.dot(base, [0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722]))
    patch, best = None, 0.0
    for i in range(len(srgb)):
        if i == dom_i or shares[i] < 0.12:
            continue
        gap = abs(float(lum[i]) - base_lum)
        if gap > 0.25 and gap > best:
            best, patch = gap, srgb[i]

    return {
        "patch": _hex(_shift(patch, dv=+0.02)) if patch is not None else None,
        "patch_contrast": round(best, 3),
        "base": _hex(base),
        "light": _hex(_shift(base, dv=+0.06, ds=-0.05)),
        "shade": _hex(_shift(base, dv=-0.05, ds=+0.03)),
        "accent": _hex(_shift(base, dv=-0.08, ds=+0.10)),
        "dark": _hex(_shift(darkest, dv=-0.02)),
        "white": _hex(_shift(brightest, dv=+0.02, ds=-0.35)),
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- geometry
def landmarks(co):
    lo, hi = co.min(axis=0), co.max(axis=0)
    span = np.where(hi - lo == 0, 1.0, hi - lo)
    n = (co - lo) / span

    up = 2                                   # Blender Z is up after stage 4
    horiz = [0, 1]
    body = horiz[int(np.argmax([span[i] for i in horiz]))]
    width = 1 - body                      # the other horizontal axis

    def cross(mask):
        if not mask.any():
            return 0.0
        s = n[mask]
        return float((s[:, width].max() - s[:, width].min()) *
                     (s[:, up].max() - s[:, up].min()))

    lowend = cross(n[:, body] < 0.08)
    highend = cross(n[:, body] > 0.92)
    head_at_zero = lowend >= highend
    ratio = (max(lowend, highend) / max(min(lowend, highend), 1e-6))

    def b(v):                                 # body coord, 0 = head
        return v if head_at_zero else 1.0 - v

    nb = b(n[:, body])
    head = n[nb < 0.22]
    info = {
        "span_studs": [round(float(v), 3) for v in span],
        "body_axis": "xyz"[body], "width_axis": "xyz"[width], "up_axis": "z",
        "head_at_axis_min": bool(head_at_zero),
        "head_end_cross_section": round(max(lowend, highend), 4),
        "tail_end_cross_section": round(min(lowend, highend), 4),
        "head_tail_ratio": round(ratio, 1),
    }
    if len(head):
        info["head_z_range"] = [round(float(head[:, up].min()), 3),
                                round(float(head[:, up].max()), 3)]
        info["head_width_range"] = [round(float(head[:, width].min()), 3),
                                    round(float(head[:, width].max()), 3)]
    nose_i = int(np.argmin(nb))
    info["nose_point"] = [round(float(v), 3) for v in n[nose_i]]
    info["nose_z"] = round(float(n[nose_i, up]), 3)

    low = n[n[:, up] < 0.05]
    info["foot_body_range"] = ([round(float(b(low[:, body]).min()), 3),
                               round(float(b(low[:, body]).max()), 3)]
                               if len(low) else None)
    ears = n[(n[:, up] > 0.90) & (nb < 0.38)]
    info["has_ears"] = bool(len(ears) > max(20, 0.004 * len(n)))
    if info["has_ears"]:
        info["ear_body"] = round(float(np.median(b(ears[:, body]))), 3)
        info["ear_z"] = round(float(np.median(ears[:, up])), 3)
    return n, body, width, up, head_at_zero, info


def build_spec(name, col, info, body, width, up, head_at_zero):
    def pt(b_, w_, h_):
        """Body/width/height in head-first coords -> the painter's x,y,z."""
        v = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
        v[body] = b_ if head_at_zero else 1.0 - b_
        v[width] = w_
        v[up] = h_
        return [round(x, 4) for x in v]

    def rad(b_, w_, h_):
        r = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
        r[body], r[width], r[up] = b_, w_, h_
        return [round(x, 4) for x in r]

    hz = info.get("head_z_range", [0.3, 0.95])
    hw = info.get("head_width_range", [0.1, 0.9])
    nose_z = info.get("nose_z", 0.72)
    head_h = max(hz[1] - hz[0], 0.15)
    side = hw[0] + (hw[1] - hw[0]) * 0.16          # just inboard of the flank
    axis_name = "xyz"[up]

    stamps = [
        {"name": "belly", "type": "band", "axis": axis_name, "max": 0.34,
         "color": col["light"], "soft": 0.20},
        {"name": "back", "type": "band", "axis": axis_name, "min": 0.86,
         "color": col["shade"], "soft": 0.14},
        {"name": "hooves", "type": "band", "axis": axis_name, "max": 0.055,
         "color": col["dark"], "soft": 0.018},
    ]

    if col.get("patch"):
        # Deterministic scatter along the body, mirrored, so a set regenerates
        # identically. Sizes and offsets are fractions of the body, not studs.
        scatter = [(0.30, 0.30, 0.55, 0.115), (0.47, 0.24, 0.72, 0.135),
                   (0.63, 0.33, 0.48, 0.100), (0.74, 0.27, 0.68, 0.120),
                   (0.20, 0.36, 0.75, 0.095), (0.55, 0.40, 0.30, 0.090),
                   (0.86, 0.31, 0.60, 0.105)]
        for i, (b_, w_, h_, r_) in enumerate(scatter):
            stamps.append({
                "name": "patch{}".format(i + 1), "type": "blob",
                "at": pt(b_, w_, h_), "r": rad(r_ * 1.15, r_ * 1.6, r_ * 1.25),
                "color": col["patch"], "soft": 0.30, "mirror": "x"})

    if info.get("has_ears"):
        stamps.append({"name": "inner_ear", "type": "blob",
                       "at": pt(info["ear_body"], side + 0.03, info["ear_z"] + 0.02),
                       "r": rad(0.10, 0.135, 0.062),
                       "color": col["accent"], "soft": 0.5, "mirror": "x"})

    facing_head = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    facing_head[body] = -1.0 if head_at_zero else 1.0
    facing_side = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    facing_side[width] = -1.0

    stamps += [
        {"name": "snout", "type": "blob", "at": pt(0.010, 0.5, nose_z),
         "r": rad(0.066, 0.232, head_h * 0.33),
         "color": col["accent"], "soft": 0.30,
         "facing": facing_head, "facing_min": 0.10},

        {"name": "nostril", "type": "blob", "at": pt(0.0, 0.418, nose_z),
         "r": rad(0.045, 0.042, 0.048),
         "color": col["dark"], "soft": 0.25,
         "facing": facing_head, "facing_min": 0.35, "mirror": "x"},

        {"name": "eye_white", "type": "blob",
         "at": pt(0.128, side, hz[0] + head_h * 0.72),
         "r": rad(0.062, 0.072, head_h * 0.095),
         "color": col["white"], "soft": 0.10,
         "facing": facing_side, "facing_min": 0.20, "mirror": "x"},

        {"name": "pupil", "type": "blob",
         "at": pt(0.122, side - 0.007, hz[0] + head_h * 0.71),
         "r": rad(0.036, 0.048, head_h * 0.055),
         "color": "#241C20", "soft": 0.10,
         "facing": facing_side, "facing_min": 0.20, "mirror": "x"},

        {"name": "brow", "type": "blob",
         "at": pt(0.142, side + 0.01, hz[0] + head_h * 0.82),
         "r": rad(0.048, 0.078, 0.014),
         "color": "#2A2024", "soft": 0.15,
         "facing": facing_side, "facing_min": 0.25, "mirror": "x"},
    ]

    return {
        "_generated": "make_paint_spec.py - FIRST PASS. Render it and look before trusting it.",
        "_asset": name,
        "_landmarks": info,
        "base": col["base"],
        "stamps": stamps,
    }


def build_prop_spec(name, col, info):
    """A prop gets its base colour and NO stamps. Deliberately.

    MEASURED 2026-08-31: before this existed, every asset went through
    build_spec, which is hard-coded cow anatomy - belly, back, hooves,
    inner_ear, snout, nostril, eye_white, pupil, brow. Run against a gold coin
    that produced **a coin with two googly eyes and eyebrows on its back face**,
    because the eye_white and pupil stamps are white and black and land wherever
    a cow's face would be.

    Every number was green while that happened: 453,632 texels painted, 0.43 UV
    coverage, exit 0. The stats measure that SOMETHING was painted, never that
    it belongs there. Only the render caught it.

    The trophy in the same batch looked fine, which is the more dangerous half:
    it is single-colour, so all nine anatomical stamps drew the same gold out of
    the concept palette and cancelled out. A prop escapes this bug exactly when
    it has nothing to lose - so "it looked right on the last prop" is not
    evidence that the next one will.

    Why flat rather than a cleverer guess: any band or patch placement for a
    generic prop is invention. A sword is not a coin is not a chest, and there
    is no anatomy to hang a rule on. A flat base colour is always plausible and
    never actively wrong, which is the correct default for something a human is
    told to look at anyway. **Multi-colour props need a hand-authored spec** -
    the file is generated once and is designed to be edited, so add the stamps
    you actually want and re-run paint_texture.py.
    """
    return {
        "_generated": ("make_paint_spec.py --preset prop. Flat base colour, no stamps. "
                       "Anatomical stamps are creature-only and put EYES on a coin. "
                       "For a multi-colour prop, hand-author the stamps below."),
        "_asset": name,
        "_landmarks": info,
        "_palette": {k: col[k] for k in ("base", "light", "shade", "dark")
                     if col.get(k)},
        "base": col["base"],
        "stamps": [],
    }


def main():
    a = args()
    mesh = Path(a.mesh).resolve()
    concept = Path(a.concept).resolve()
    co, _uv, _ln, tv, _tl = P.load_mesh(mesh)
    n, body, width, up, head_at_zero, info = landmarks(co)

    # A prop has no head, so the head-end gate is not just unnecessary here, it
    # is unanswerable - and before this branch existed it was silently answered
    # anyway and used to place a face.
    if a.preset == "prop":
        srgb, shares, lum = palette(concept, a.clusters)
        col = choose_colours(srgb, shares, lum)
        spec = build_prop_spec(a.name, col, info)
        out = Path(a.out).resolve()
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(json.dumps(spec, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        print("[spec] PROP: flat base {}, no anatomical stamps".format(col["base"]))
        print("[spec] hand-author stamps in the file if this prop needs more than "
              "one colour")
        print("[spec] wrote {}".format(out))
        return 0

    if a.head_end == "min":
        head_at_zero = True
    elif a.head_end == "max":
        head_at_zero = False
    elif info["head_tail_ratio"] < a.min_confidence:
        raise SystemExit(
            "[spec] REFUSING TO GUESS the head end: cross-section ratio is only "
            "{}x (need {}x). This heuristic already picked the WRONG end on the "
            "cow at 2.3x. Render scripts/axes_probe.py, look at it, and pass "
            "--head-end min or --head-end max.".format(
                info["head_tail_ratio"], a.min_confidence))
    info["head_at_axis_min"] = bool(head_at_zero)
    info["head_end_source"] = ("explicit:" + a.head_end) if a.head_end != "auto"         else "auto ({}x)".format(info["head_tail_ratio"])

    srgb, shares, lum = palette(concept, a.clusters)
    col = choose_colours(srgb, shares, lum)

    spec = build_spec(a.name, col, info, body, width, up, head_at_zero)
    out = Path(a.out).resolve()
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(spec, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print("[spec] body axis {}, head at {} end".format(
        info["body_axis"], "min" if head_at_zero else "max"))
    print("[spec] base {}  light {}  shade {}  dark {}".format(
        col["base"], col["light"], col["shade"], col["dark"]))
    print("[spec] ears: {} | patches: {}".format(
        "yes" if info.get("has_ears") else "no",
        "{} (contrast {})".format(col["patch"], col["patch_contrast"])
        if col.get("patch") else "no second colour found"))
    print("[spec] head end source: {}".format(info["head_end_source"]))
    print("[spec] wrote {}".format(out))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Stage 4: a 600k-face generated mesh -> a Roblox-legal MeshPart plus a normal map.

Runs inside Blender:

    blender --background --python scripts/mesh_pipeline.py -- \
        --input work/high.glb --outdir work/out --target-tris 9000

The whole design is one sentence: Roblox caps a MeshPart at 20,000 triangles and
the real working budget is under 10,000, which against 600,000 is a 60:1 cut, so
the detail has to be MOVED into a normal map rather than thrown away.

Order matters and is not arbitrary:
    import -> join -> normalise scale -> duplicate -> decimate -> smart UV ->
    smooth shade -> bake high onto low -> export low + PNG

Scale is normalised BEFORE the duplicate so the two meshes share a coordinate
frame; bake a cage across two differently-scaled objects and you get garbage that
looks like a UV problem.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import bpy


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# argv
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    # Blender passes its own flags first; everything after a bare -- is ours.
    argv = sys.argv
    argv = argv[argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in argv else []

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True, help=".glb/.gltf/.obj/.fbx high-poly")
    ap.add_argument("--outdir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target-tris", type=int, default=9000,
                    help="Roblox hard cap is 20000; under 10000 is the working budget")
    ap.add_argument("--texture-size", type=int, default=1024,
                    help="SurfaceAppearance caps at 1024; larger is downscaled on upload")
    ap.add_argument("--decimate-mode", choices=["collapse", "planar"], default="collapse",
                    help="collapse for organic, planar for hard surface")
    ap.add_argument("--planar-angle", type=float, default=5.0,
                    help="degrees, planar mode only")
    ap.add_argument("--target-studs", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="scale so the longest axis is this many studs (0 = leave alone)")
    ap.add_argument("--uv-margin", type=float, default=0.003,
                    help="island margin, charged PER ISLAND; 0.02 wastes most of a "
                         "1024 map on a mesh with many islands")
    ap.add_argument("--uv-angle", type=float, default=66.0, help="smart project angle limit, degrees")
    ap.add_argument("--cage-extrusion", type=float, default=-1.0,
                    help="<0 auto-scales from model size")
    ap.add_argument("--bake-margin", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=1,
                    help="a normal bake is a geometric projection; 1 is correct and fast")
    ap.add_argument("--weld-threshold", type=float, default=1e-5,
                    help="merge-by-distance threshold used to undo the importer's vertex split")
    ap.add_argument("--min-part-frac", type=float, default=0.002,
                    help="drop loose parts under this share of faces before decimating")
    ap.add_argument("--remesh-voxel", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="voxel-remesh the low copy first, voxel = this x longest "
                         "dimension (0 = off). For meshes where collapse stalls")
    ap.add_argument("--no-bake", action="store_true", help="decimate and unwrap only")
    return ap.parse_args(argv)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# scene helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def reset_scene() -> None:
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)


def import_any(path: Path) -> list[bpy.types.Object]:
    """Import and return only the objects this call added.

    Diffing the object set beats trusting the selection, which importers leave in
    inconsistent states. Blender 4.x renamed the OBJ importer, so route by suffix.
    """
    before = set(bpy.data.objects)
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix in (".glb", ".gltf"):
        bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=str(path))
    elif suffix == ".obj":
        bpy.ops.wm.obj_import(filepath=str(path))
